title: Giving, taking and holding
intro: A cluster of high-frequency verbs that English keeps apart but Spanish distributes differently. Note especially poner versus meter, and dejar, which covers leaving, letting and stopping.

entries.en: to leave (behind); to let, to allow; to stop doing
entries.note: dejar de + infinitive is to stop doing something: dejé de fumar.

ex.es: Dejé las llaves en la mesa.
ex.en: I left the keys on the table.
They won't let me in.

ex.es: Dejó de llover a las cinco.
ex.en: It stopped raining at five.

entries.note: poner is to place on a surface; meter is to put inside something.

ex.es: Metió la ropa en la maleta.
ex.en: He put the clothes in the suitcase.

entries.en: to take out; to get, to obtain
entries.note: sacar una foto is to take a photo; sacar buena nota to get a good mark.

ex.en: Take the rubbish out, please.

ex.es: Sacó el pasaporte en una semana.
ex.en: He got his passport in a week.

entries.note: See unit 2. In Latin America it is the default for both.

ex.en: Take a seat, please.
We had a drink after work.

entries.en: to grab, to take hold of; to catch
entries.note: The safe Latin American alternative to coger — see the warning in unit 2.

ex.en: Hold the bag tightly.
I caught the last bus.

entries.en: to let go of, to release

ex.en: Let go of my arm.

entries.note: el regalo is the present. Spanish has a separate verb where English says give a present.

ex.en: They gave me a book as a present.

entries.en: to send; (mandar) to order, to be in charge

ex.es: Te mando la dirección por mensaje.
ex.en: I'll send you the address by message.
She's the one in charge here.

entries.en: to receive; to welcome, to see (a visitor)

ex.en: I received your letter yesterday.

ex.es: El doctor recibe de nueve a una.
ex.en: The doctor sees patients from nine to one.

entries.note: volver is to come back yourself; devolver is to give a thing back.

ex.en: Give me the book back when you can.

entries.en: to lose; to miss (a train, a chance)

ex.es: Perdí el paraguas en el taxi.
ex.en: I lost my umbrella in the taxi.

ex.es: Perdimos el vuelo por el tráfico.
ex.en: We missed the flight because of the traffic.

entries.note: See unit 27 for the computing sense.

ex.es: Guarda esto en un lugar seguro.
ex.en: Keep this somewhere safe.

entries.note: usar lentes is to wear glasses — usar covers habitual wearing, llevar what you have on today.

ex.en: Use this knife, it cuts better.
She's worn glasses since she was a girl.

entries.en: to serve; to be useful, to work
entries.note: no sirve means it's no good, it doesn't work. ¿para qué sirve? is what's it for?

ex.es: Sirvieron la cena a las nueve.
ex.en: They served dinner at nine.
This key is no good.

entries.note: ayudar a + infinitive: me ayudó a cargar las bolsas. la ayuda is help.

ex.en: Shall I help you with that?
I haven't bought the presents yet.

entries.note: The most useful noun in the language when you don't know the word. otra cosa is something else.

ex.es: Deja tus cosas en el cuarto.
ex.en: Leave your things in the room.
They found several old objects.

ex.es: ¿Cuál es el objeto de la reunión?
ex.en: What is the purpose of the meeting?

entries.note: la pieza is a component or a room; el trozo a chunk.

ex.en: Would you like a piece of cake?

entries.note: en alguna parte means somewhere; por otra parte means on the other hand.

ex.es: La primera parte es la más difícil.
ex.en: The first part is the hardest.
I saw it somewhere.
